newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU council to respect ECB independence - Frenchsour.
newsitem.headline: EMU council to respect ECB independence - Frenchsour.

text.p: An economic council being sought by France to co-ordinate economic policies among countries in European monetary union would fully respect the independence of the European Central Bank (ECB), a finance ministry source said on Monday.
France's call for such a council had raised some fears it might try to influence the policies of the ECB.

"We have always said France wanted an informal stability council, respecting the principles of subsidiarity and fully respecting the independence of the central bank," the source said. "There has never been a debate on this question and there will not be," he added.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Friday that the creation of a political power to control the European Central Bank would be against the Maastricht treaty.
French officials say, however, that the idea of a stability council is not to influence or control the central bank, but to allow countries sharing a common currency to co-ordinate policies.
